documents.title: Loose Diamond Evaluation in Downtown LA: What to Prepare

body.alt: Three large oval polished diamonds arranged in a green jewelry tray
body.caption: Three large oval polished diamonds arranged in a green jewelry tray. Illustrative jewelry image; not actual inventory or a representation of verified origin, purity or grading.

children.text: Organize stones one at a time

For several loose diamonds, make an item list and keep each stone in a separate suitable gem container. Match its paperwork to the list. This helps avoid confusing similar-looking stones or repeating a report's information for the wrong diamond.

Write down the known shape and report number. Distinguish a documented carat weight from an estimate. If you also have a ring or pendant you might sell, keep it intact instead of removing its stone to create another loose diamond.
Bring the records you already have
Useful records can include a grading report, receipt, prior appraisal and information about damage or recutting. For GIA paperwork, use
Report Check
to consult the available record.

Ask how the report is matched to the actual stone. If the report is missing or you are uncertain about a number, explain the gap. Do not pay for new documentation solely because you assume every buyer requires it.
Prepare quality questions without assigning grades
GIA's quality factors
provide a useful vocabulary for carat, color, clarity and cut. Shape and millimeter measurements add further detail to the description.
The
diamond grading chart guide
explains the abbreviations and scales you may encounter on a report.

body.alt: Close view of a stone being inspected through a loupe
body.caption: Close view of a stone being inspected through a loupe.

children.text: Ask which characteristics are confirmed by existing records and which need examination. Share known chips, abrasions or treatments. A diamond's weight alone does not establish its identity, quality or an offer.
If the report records fluorescence, ask how it affects this particular stone's appearance and offer.
GIA explains that fluorescence can affect appearance or have no visible effect
; its presence alone does not establish a fixed discount.
Our
large natural diamond guide
covers substantial stones as well as smaller diamonds of any shape. Keep a single stone's weight separate from totals for a collection.
Say what you need from the evaluation
A purchase proposal and a formal valuation report are different services.
GIA explains why a grading report does not assign monetary value
. An insurance or other formal appraisal also needs a stated purpose and scope.
If a third party needs a document, ask about its requirements first. Tell the provider what report is expected rather than assuming that a buyer's offer will meet that need. The
evaluation-versus-appraisal guide
explains the distinction.
Compare the offer against your item list

Check which stones are included and whether the amount is final or subject to additional work. For several items, ask for enough detail to understand the proposal before deciding to sell part or all of the collection.

Confirm any outstanding costs, the duration of the offer and payment arrangements. If you remove an item from the sale, request a revised amount. A quote for a different origin, grade or set of items cannot settle the comparison.
Contact the Downtown Los Angeles location

Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds buys natural polished diamonds of any size and shape. We do not buy laboratory-grown diamonds or rough and uncut material. Tell us what the documentation says if origin is uncertain.
Call
or
contact us
to arrange a visit to 617 S. Hill Street, Los Angeles, CA 90014. Our
diamond-buying service
offers cash, bank wire or business-check payment for agreed purchases.

documents.title: How to Value Estate Jewelry: Inventory, Materials & Records

body.alt: A substantial three-stone diamond ring beside a closed jeweler's loupe on a warm gray evaluation pad
body.caption: A substantial three-stone diamond ring beside a closed jeweler's loupe on a warm gray evaluation pad. Illustrative estate-style jewelry; not authenticated age, actual inventory or grading evidence.

children.text: Create a simple inventory before assigning values

Give each piece a short identifier and photograph it from several angles. Keep matching earrings, chains and pendants associated with one another, and note any detached parts. Separate observations from assumptions: “blue stone” is more useful than an unsupported claim that it is sapphire.

cells: Ring A, necklace B or another clear label
Letters, numbers and symbols exactly as seen
Missing pieces, damage and known repairs
Receipts, reports, appraisals and maker information
Documented facts, with family recollections labeled separately

children.text: Keep materials and complete-piece features separate

A collection may contain precious metals, plated items, costume jewelry and pieces whose materials are unknown. Do not assume that everything is gold because it came from the same jewelry box. Let examination establish which materials are present.

body.alt: Assorted colored gemstone rings in a display tray
body.caption: Assorted colored gemstone rings in a display tray.

children.text: For gold jewelry, the relevant metal weight and purity must be distinguished from stones and other components. A complete piece also warrants consideration of its design and condition.
GIA’s estate jewelry guide
highlights examination for damage, missing stones and evidence of repairs.
Ask what supports stone and maker identification

Bring existing laboratory reports and ask which stones they describe. Natural origin and treatment status are separate details; an identification should not assume that every natural gemstone is untreated. Record what the examiner established and any limits on the assessment.
If a report describes a diamond, our
diamond grading chart guide
explains its color, clarity and cut terminology so you can prepare more specific evaluation questions.

A maker’s mark or period-style design can guide research, but it is not a substitute for authentication. Ask what supports the attribution and date. Avoid dismantling a possible antique or signed piece before its complete design has been considered; see the
antique gold evaluation guide
Define the purpose of a requested value
The
Appraisal Foundation’s jewelry guide
explains that a credible appraisal identifies the items, intended use, value definition and relevant date. Establish those requirements before commissioning a report.

A buyer’s current purchase amount answers a different practical question: what is offered for the stated items under the stated terms? Do not convert an old appraisal into that amount using a fixed percentage. Our
inherited jewelry documentation guide
helps you choose the right next step.
Preserve the collection for evaluation
Store pieces separately and avoid experimenting with cleaning on unfamiliar materials.
GIA’s care guidance
notes that gemstones and treatments can require different handling. Ask before paying for restoration intended only to improve a sale price.
For a purchase evaluation,
contact Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds
at 310-663-1340 or visit 617 S. Hill Street, Los Angeles, CA 90014. Our
estate jewelry service
can discuss the collection you have and the information needed for an offer.
Can I value an entire jewelry box by its total weight?
No. Different materials and individual pieces need identification. A combined scale weight does not establish the relevant precious-metal content or complete-piece value.
Should I discard items that look like costume jewelry?
Keep uncertain items identifiable until you know what they are. Appearance alone is not a reliable way to sort a collection by material or potential significance.

documents.title: 14K Gold Price Per Gram: Estimating Jewelry Value

body.alt: Gold bars displayed with United States banknotes
body.caption: Gold bars displayed with United States banknotes. Representative editorial image; not a record of this business’s inventory, staff, prices or verified material grades.

children.text: Calculate the gold content before comparing prices

To estimate the metal value of 14K gold, multiply the pure-gold price per gram by 14 ÷ 24, or approximately 0.5833. Then multiply by the net weight of the 14K alloy. This estimates contained gold value; a purchase offer also depends on the actual item and the buyer's terms.
14K means 14 parts gold in a 24-part alloy. A 585 fineness mark indicates 58.5% gold and is commonly associated with 14K jewelry. The
World Gold Council's explanation of karat and fineness
describes the small distinction between nominal 14K and 585. Use the purity established during the evaluation when comparing a real offer. Our guide to
14K marks, color and construction
explains what these descriptions tell you.

A marking is a starting clue: stamps can wear, repairs can introduce other metals, and separate components may have different purities. Ask how purity will be checked and whether a proposed test could mark the piece.
GIA’s 1992 study of gold-testing methods
provides historical background on touchstone, electronic and X-ray fluorescence (XRF) testing and their limitations.
Convert a troy-ounce reference into grams
If a gold-price reference is quoted in dollars per troy ounce, first divide it by 31.1034768 to obtain dollars per gram of pure gold. A troy ounce is different from an ordinary household ounce. The
NIST mass reference
provides the conversion.
Estimated contained gold value = net alloy weight in grams × tested gold fraction × pure-gold price per gram.
The
World Gold Council's gold-price data

offers market references. Check the currency, unit, date, and whether a displayed value is an average or benchmark. It is not a binding offer for your jewelry, and this article does not display a live buying rate.
Worked example: a 25-gram 14K bracelet

Assume a plain bracelet contains 25 grams of 14K alloy after accounting for any non-gold components. Its estimated pure-gold content is 25 × 14 ÷ 24 = approximately 14.58 grams. Multiply that amount by the current reference price per gram of pure gold to obtain a metal-content estimate.

body.alt: Gold jewelry arranged beside a digital scale and testing tools
body.caption: Gold jewelry arranged beside a digital scale and testing tools.

children.text: These are calculated metal quantities, not promised payouts. A bracelet's total weight may also include diamonds, non-gold springs, or other materials. A household scale and a visible stamp can help you prepare questions, but they do not establish a tested net gold weight.
Understand the difference between a reference and an offer

A metal-only purchase offer can reflect testing, processing, refining, resale costs, and the buyer's margin. Jewelry with a desirable maker, significant stones, or collectible features may instead deserve evaluation as a complete piece. Do not add an intact jewelry resale estimate to its full metal value; that could count the same material twice. To distinguish a retail receipt or replacement appraisal from a current offer, read
what to expect for gold jewelry

For heavy Cuban chains and bracelets, ask about construction as well as weight. Hollow links and solid links can look similar while containing different amounts of metal. If diamonds are present, ask how the stones affect both the weight calculation and the offer. See our
14K chain guide
for these item-specific checks.
Compare 14K gold offers on the same basis

Keep the same pieces together when requesting comparisons. Ask each buyer to state the tested purity, weight unit, weight used, whether stones are included, any charges, and the final payment. If one quote uses grams and another uses pennyweights, ask for matching units before comparing rates. Use the
gold-offer comparison worksheet
to record the same details for each buyer.
An estimate given before examination may change if the item differs from the description. Compare final amounts for the actual jewelry, not only an advertised per-gram figure. Our
gold-valuation guide
covers the broader factors behind an offer.
Arrange a 14K gold evaluation in Downtown Los Angeles

Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds buys 14K jewelry, scrap gold, Cuban chains and bracelets with or without diamonds, gold coins, and silver coins at 617 S. Hill Street, Los Angeles, CA 90014. Single pieces, large quantities, and high-value transactions are welcome.
Keep matching pieces and existing reports together. The
Downtown LA gold-evaluation checklist
covers what to bring. Call
to discuss a substantial lot and your preferred payment method. Payment is available by cash, bank wire, or business check. Visit our
gold-buying page
for the full buying scope.
Are equal weights of 14K white, yellow and rose gold worth the same?
At the same tested gold fraction, they contain the same amount of gold. A complete piece's offer may still differ because of its stones, maker, condition, or resale demand. Read more about
white gold's alloy and finish
Should I remove stones before weighing my jewelry?
No. Have the intact jewelry evaluated first and ask how non-gold weight is accounted for. Removing stones can damage the setting and make an evaluation of the complete piece more difficult.
Can this formula tell me the best day to sell?
No. It explains metal content using a stated price reference; it does not predict markets. Decide using an actual offer, the items you own, and your circumstances.

documents.title: How to Sell a Rolex in Los Angeles: A Preparation Checklist

body.alt: Rose-gold Rolex Day-Date-style watch with an olive dial and President bracelet on pale suede
body.caption: Rose-gold Rolex Day-Date-style watch with an olive dial and President bracelet on pale suede. Illustrative watch concept; not actual inventory, an exact model reference or authentication evidence.

children.text: 1. Make a simple item record

Write down the model or reference shown in your records, the accessories you have and any known damage or alterations. If you do not know the reference or production date, say so. A remembered purchase year should not become an unsupported manufacturing date.
The
official Rolex collections
can help you recognize model-family names. Current catalogue images cannot establish an older watch's exact reference, originality, authenticity or purchase value.
Record the watch's present condition for your own records. Avoid publicly sharing full identifying numbers or personal details from warranty documents when seeking an initial conversation.
2. Gather the complete package

Include spare bracelet links, the box, warranty papers, receipts and service invoices if available. Keep unrelated accessories separate. Missing papers do not prevent you from asking for a purchase evaluation.
For an inherited watch, keep family information distinct from documented history and confirm your authority to decide about a sale. The
vintage Rolex guide
covers uncertain history and component originality.
3. Preserve its current condition

Do not open the case, force the crown or arrange cosmetic restoration just to prepare for an offer. If the watch is damaged or has stopped, describe that before visiting. Ask whether an as-is evaluation is appropriate before spending money on repairs.

body.alt: Two-tone Rolex Daytona with black dial
body.caption: Two-tone Rolex Daytona with black dial.

children.text: Rolex's manufacturer guidance
provides care and servicing information. The condition of an individual older watch still matters; a general cleaning instruction should not be treated as proof it is currently water-resistant.
4. Agree on the examination

Ask who will handle the watch, whether opening or additional testing is proposed, and how any time away from you will be documented. Get an itemized receipt if the watch must be left for further work.
A purchase proposal is not automatically a formal authentication report.
Rolex Certified Pre-Owned
is a separate manufacturer programme, not a generic label for every used Rolex evaluation.
5. Compare the amount and its conditions

Ask for the offered amount and the precise items included. Note any unresolved inspection condition, charge or expiration of the proposal. Compare another offer on the same basis if you want a second opinion.
For a gold Rolex, request consideration as a complete watch before a metal-only calculation. The
gold Rolex guide
explains why case and bracelet materials do not replace reference-level evaluation.
For a Day-Date, the
reference and bracelet evaluation guide
explains which details and records to bring.
6. Confirm payment before the handover
Choose a payment method, confirm the timing and keep the purchase record. Do not assume a preliminary estimate has become an accepted transaction. Our
Los Angeles Rolex buyer page
explains how to start the local evaluation.
For an in-person purchase evaluation,
contact Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds
at 617 S. Hill Street, Los Angeles, CA 90014, or call
. Payment for agreed purchases is available by cash, bank wire or business check; confirm the arrangements before accepting.

documents.title: Selling Inherited Jewelry Without Pressure: A Practical Guide

body.alt: Substantial platinum rivière necklace of large graduated cushion-cut diamonds on slate velvet
body.caption: Substantial platinum rivière necklace of large graduated cushion-cut diamonds on slate velvet. Illustrative estate-style jewelry; not authenticated age, actual inventory or grading evidence.

children.text: Decide what you are comfortable considering

You do not need to make one decision about an entire inheritance. Set aside pieces you want to keep, identify those you are comfortable discussing and leave uncertain items in a separate group. A photograph or written family history may also be worth preserving independently of a sale.

People attach different meanings to inherited jewelry. Keeping a piece, selling it or waiting can each be a reasonable personal choice. If other people share ownership or decision-making responsibility, resolve that before committing items to a transaction.
Clarify the appointment and service terms

Describe the collection when contacting a buyer. Ask what to bring, how the appointment works and whether any proposed service has a charge. A no-obligation purchase discussion should leave the sale decision with you, but it should not be confused with an agreement for separate paid work.

body.alt: Assorted colored gemstone rings in a display tray
body.caption: Assorted colored gemstone rings in a display tray.

children.text: The
Appraisal Foundation’s guide

distinguishes the scope and intended use of a formal appraisal. If your purpose is insurance or estate documentation, establish that requirement rather than assuming a buyer’s offer supplies the document you need.
Bring an organized collection

Keep matching jewelry and any detached components together. Bring existing receipts, reports and repair history, and tell the evaluator which items you are considering for sale. Label information you do not know as unknown.
If your collection includes a Rolex, the
local watch-buyer guide
helps you compare evaluation arrangements. For diamond pieces, the
diamond identification and selling guide
explains what to establish before discussing value.
GIA’s estate jewelry guidance
highlights condition and repairs as useful details to examine. Our
inventory guide
provides a simple way to record those observations without trying to price every piece yourself.
Ask for an offer you can understand

cells: The exact pieces covered by the amount
Whether keeping selected items changes the remaining offer
Any conditions that could change the number
How long the offer remains available
The final amount, method and expected availability

children.text: If something is unclear, ask for an explanation before accepting. Keep a written summary when comparing offers. A decision to wait does not require a buyer to keep a price available indefinitely, so record the offer’s actual terms.
Take the next step that fits your purpose
You may request a purchase evaluation now, seek required appraisal documentation or wait while you discuss the collection with family. The
inherited jewelry valuation guide
explains how those purposes differ.
Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds offers an
estate jewelry buying service
at 617 S. Hill Street, Los Angeles, CA 90014.
Contact us
at 310-663-1340 to describe your collection. Our diamond buying is for natural cut and polished diamonds in any size or shape; we do not buy laboratory-grown, uncut or rough diamonds.
Can I decide to keep a piece after hearing an offer?
Make your decision before accepting the transaction. If you remove an item from a proposed collection sale, ask for the revised scope and amount.
Does no obligation to sell mean every appraisal service is free?
No. A purchase discussion and a separately commissioned appraisal are different services. Confirm any proposed charges and deliverables before authorizing work.

body.alt: Yellow-gold Rolex Day-Date-style watch with a champagne dial and diamond bezel
body.caption: Yellow-gold Rolex Day-Date-style watch with a champagne dial and diamond bezel. Illustrative watch concept; not actual inventory, an exact model reference or authentication evidence.

children.text: Identify the Day-Date you actually have

Record the reference from available documents and describe the dial, bezel, case and bracelet. Avoid choosing a reference solely because a current online image looks similar. Earlier examples and later modifications may need additional research.
The
official Rolex Day-Date collection

describes the model family and its precious-metal configurations. The President bracelet is closely associated with this collection, but a nickname is not a complete description of an individual watch.
Include the bracelet in the evaluation
Bring detached links and note any replacement clasp or bracelet work you know about. Ask how length, wear, repairs and the relationship of the bracelet to the case are being considered.
A full-watch weight includes non-gold components. Do not multiply that weight by a pure-gold price or assume every fitted component matches the case material. The
gold Rolex selling guide
discusses complete-watch assessment.
Separate configuration from later changes

Disclose dial, bezel or diamond-setting changes if known. Ask the evaluator to distinguish original components, manufacturer service replacements and aftermarket alterations. The presence of gemstones does not by itself establish factory setting or their natural origin.

body.alt: Gold Rolex Daytona with green dial
body.caption: Gold Rolex Daytona with green dial.

children.text: Do not open the case yourself to check a movement. A familiar logo, serial number or substantial feel cannot authenticate the complete watch. Our
Rolex authentication guide
explains the limits of visual shortcuts.
Use service history and condition together
Bring service invoices, including any description of parts replaced. A prior service date does not guarantee present operation or water resistance. Describe current problems honestly.
Before arranging polishing or repair solely for a sale, discuss an evaluation in the watch's present condition.
Rolex's care and service information
is the primary source for manufacturer support.
Compare an offer without assuming an investment return

A luxury watch can rise or fall in resale value. Neither its precious-metal content nor brand name creates a guaranteed resale floor for the amount you paid. Gold price changes also do not translate into a fixed percentage change in a complete Day-Date offer.
Compare the same reference, condition, accessories and sale terms. An advertised watch with a warranty or
Rolex Certified Pre-Owned programme
coverage is not equivalent to every privately presented example.

Review the
